summary: Unit tests thoroughly cover the LicenseChecker module functions with good edge cases and mocking, but CRITICALLY FAIL the primary requirement: 'ALL TESTS MUST RUN THROUGH ACT.' The task explicitly mandates act-based workflow execution testing with output capture to act-result.txt and exact-value assertions—none of this exists. Workflow.Structure.Tests.ps1 only parses YAML and validates actionlint; it does NOT execute `act push`, capture output, verify exit codes, or create the required artifact. Invoke-LicenseCheck.ps1 (the entry point) has zero integration tests. Without act execution tests, the suite cannot validate that the CI/CD pipeline works, cannot verify exit codes (0/1/2), cannot test environment variables (FAIL_ON_DENIED), and cannot catch real-world workflow failures. The unit tests are well-designed but insufficient—they test the module in isolation, not the actual deployment pipeline that is the core deliverable.
